loop.top3_why: The weighted combination (pool_full, weights w1) delivers the lowest validation score and shows the most stable per‑window performance (0.727, 0.649, 0.632). It uses all 19 models but relies on weights derived from a meta‑model trained on other series, which mitigates overfitting to this single series while still capturing systematic differences among models. Given the series’ strong trend dominance and the diagnostic recommendation for a robust combination, this weighted approach is expected to generalize better than the median strategies, which either include all models (median full pool) or a subset (median pool2) and exhibit higher per‑window variance.
loop.top3_why_not: Median full pool has a higher overall score (0.6735) and a noticeably higher error in window 1 (0.742), indicating less stability. Median pool2, while robust, relies on only seven models and shows extreme variance across windows (0.873 in window 1), suggesting it may over‑react to a single window’s idiosyncrasies. Both median strategies are therefore less suitable than the weighted baseline for a trend‑dominated, non‑stationary series with unstable model rankings.
